reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one runtime change: Cursor's imported copies of Notifai's Claude Code hooks (a bare `notifai` once Cursor drops exec-form `args`, or a shell-form `hook ... --harness claude-code`) now end silently with exit 0 when Cursor's hook environment is present, in the native launcher on macOS and Linux and at the runtime entry and hook guard elsewhere; the guard also recognises the IDE's empty CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR. A bare `notifai` at a terminal still opens the app and elsewhere still prints help, so the README's description holds. No hook definition, command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for the Cursor activation follow-up. It is now sent at most once per conversation, recorded by conversation id outside session state, because the Cursor SDK starts and ends a session around every turn and each new session re-armed it. Its text now opens by saying it is an automatic activation not from the User, carries the same root ownership and effective guidance, and closes by asking the agent to evaluate the turn it just finished and then repeat its previous reply exactly instead of acknowledging the activation, since hosts such as T3 Code show only that reply. The README and the Cursor harness reference say the same. No command, flag, readiness id, hook definition or guidance topic changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for one comment-only change: the note in the hook builder that explains why the Session Child's attend handler stays a separate asynchronous handler now records the harness behaviour behind it (a process left by a synchronous hook is reparented to init, the hub refuses it as not the harness's child, Codex ends a session by killing its async hooks and never kills such a process, Claude Code kills neither and does not time out a backgrounded hook). No hook definition, command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for two fixes. A Codex hook refresh keeps the revision its handlers already carry, so an update that adds one handler leaves every unchanged handler byte-identical and Codex asks the User to review only the new or changed one; the updates reference already says changed handlers can require /hooks approval, which stays true, and the activation proof still accepts a callback from the healthy definition present. Rollback, a stable downgrade and an npm switch to a release before 13.1.0-beta.3 now rewrite exec-form Claude Code hooks to shell form before that release becomes active, and activate or install nothing when that fails, reporting it with `notifai doctor --json` as the recovery command; agents still run the same update and rollback commands and follow the reported recovery command, so no command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed. Earlier on main, kept: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms for two small CLI changes. `config set --project` for a key that widens network trust (media_origins, approve_origins) now gives the trust-specific refusal wherever it runs, including outside a Git checkout, instead of the generic shared-settings refusal; both already name `--local`. `notifai config` for humans aligns each group's names on their own and continues a long value under itself, so no row is wider than the terminal; the plain and JSON forms are unchanged. No agent-facing behaviour, command, flag, readiness id or guidance wording changed.
